---
title: "Download"
subtitle: "Where to get DeskPets"
---

DeskPets for Windows comes as a normal installer. You don't need Python or anything else installed.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Get it
**[Download the latest installer](https://github.com/Suyash-Naik/DeskPets/releases/latest)** from the GitHub releases page. Under *Assets*, pick `DeskPets-Setup-<version>.exe`.
:::

## Installing

1. Run `DeskPets-Setup-<version>.exe` and follow the steps. It installs for your user only, so it doesn't ask for administrator rights.
2. Two options on the way, both off unless you tick them: starting DeskPets when you sign in to Windows, and launching it when the installer closes.
3. Otherwise start it from the Start Menu. Right-click the tray icon to quit.

Your settings are kept in `%APPDATA%\LC-pet-stat`, and uninstalling leaves them alone, so reinstalling or upgrading keeps your pets where you left them.

## Things you may notice

- **Windows SmartScreen may warn you.** The installer isn't code-signed yet, so Windows shows "Windows protected your PC" for new, unrecognised downloads. Choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*, if you trust the download. You can check it hasn't been altered by comparing its hash with the one on the release page:

  ```powershell
  Get-FileHash .\DeskPets-Setup-<version>.exe -Algorithm SHA256
  ```

- **The first start can be slow.** Right after installing, Windows scans the new files, and the pets can take a little while to appear. Later starts are quick. Starting it twice in the meantime gives you two pets.

## Requirements

- **Windows.** macOS and Linux aren't supported.
- **An NVIDIA GPU is optional.** Without one, DeskPets still runs, but the GPU rows and the GPU-temperature trigger for the grumpy animation aren't available. See [Known limitations](/project/known-limitations.qmd).

## Run it from source

If you'd rather run it from the code, use [pixi](https://pixi.sh), which sets up the right Python and libraries. [Getting started](/guide/getting-started.qmd) walks through it. How the installer is built is described in [How it works](/internals/how-it-works.qmd#building-the-app).

## Follow along

Progress is tracked on [GitHub](https://github.com/Suyash-Naik/DeskPets/issues), and the plan is on the [Roadmap](roadmap.qmd). Watching the repository there is the quickest way to hear when a new release appears.
